summary.headline: Jai Balaji Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled (+93%) to a ~9% margin, while DI pipe demand stays subdued.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 93% with margin around 9% (from 5%), and PAT up roughly threefold (about 192%) with PAT margin near 5% (from 2%). Profitability gains were attributed to better realisations in ferroalloys and pig iron, higher commodity volumes and cost control. DI pipe demand remains weak on slow government fund releases, although management expects an uptick by FY28 as JJM funds are used. Capex of about INR1,112 crore is nearly complete, with blast furnace, sinter and ferroalloy additions targeted for commissioning by end-Q3 FY27. Net term debt fell to INR145 crore at H1 FY27 from INR169 crore at FY26 end.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 28% of Q2 FY27 revenue; margin cited at 15-16%. Capacity rising from 1.66 lakh to 1.9 lakh tpa, adding 25,000-30,000 tonnes; utilisation targeted above 90%.

segments.name: DI pipes
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded to more than 5.5 lakh tpa, with current utilisation around 30-40%. Order book about 80,000-90,000 tonnes, roughly 50% index-linked with price-variation clause; exports minimal.

segments.name: Pig iron and commodities (billets, TMT)
segments.commentary: Production improved in Q2; surplus DI output is sold as pig iron at a reasonable margin. Commodities priced on spot with 15-20 day pass-through lag.

segments.name: Blast furnace and sinter
segments.commentary: Blast furnace capacity going from 6.3 to 7.5 lakh tpa; sinter from 9 to about 12 lakh tpa. Management expects blast furnace EBITDA to rise 25-30% on the enhanced module.

guidance_outlook: Blast furnace, sinter and specialised ferroalloy capacities targeted for commissioning by end-Q3 FY27; overall capex of INR1,112 crore nearly complete, funded mainly by internal accruals.

Ferroalloy share of revenue expected to rise from 28% to 30-31%, with absolute ferroalloy revenue of about INR400 crore; management cited incremental revenue potential of INR400-500 crore from the ferroalloy expansion.
Sustainable overall EBITDA margin seen moving from ~9% toward 10-10.5% as new blast furnace comes on stream.
Gross debt guided down from INR188 crore to about INR140 crore by March 2027, and to INR100-110 crore depending on cash surplus.
Working capital packing-credit cost from HDFC expected to fall from about 12% to 7%.
Management expects DI pipe demand to improve in FY28 or just before, as JJM funds are used before its March 2028 timeline.
Raw material (thermal and coking coal) cost increases expected to hit Q3 and Q4; management expects most to be passed on to customers.
About one quarter of capex-related hiatus before the next phase of investment is announced; West Bengal investments are at the planning stage at group level.
capex_capacity: DI pipes capacity expanded to more than 5.5 lakh tpa; utilisation currently 30-40%, with management saying 60-70% is needed for economics.
Specialised ferroalloys capacity rising from 1.66 lakh to 1.9 lakh tpa.
Blast furnace capacity rising from 6.3 lakh to 7.5 lakh tpa; sinter capacity from 9 lakh to about 12 lakh tpa.
Two to three major modules still pending completion; capex completion targeted between end-November and January 2027.
Three dedicated railway sidings support logistics.
demand_pricing: DI pipe demand subdued for about four to five quarters on slow government spending and fund releases; inquiry pipeline above 2 lakh tonnes, but contractors reluctant to commit further funds.
Management says the DI pricing 'bloodbath' occurred in the prior quarter due to excess industry inventory; it now sees marginal price improvement as the industry rationalises capacity.
Ferroalloy realisations rose over recent quarters; management does not expect further realisation gains and aims to sustain current margins.

Exports to 40+ countries; India gaining share in specialty ferroalloys, with long-term customer contracts and stock in Europe and the US. Freight costs elevated due to geopolitics, which limits DI exports.
Budget: about INR16,500 crore spent in H1 out of INR67,000 crore annual budget for the JJM-related allocation as cited on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the enhanced capacities to reach optimum utilisation, and the incremental revenue and EBITDA over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Two to three major modules are pending. Blast furnace EBITDA is expected to rise 25-30% with the enhanced module, and the ferroalloy module adds capacity and integrates partly non-integrated operations. No numerical guidance beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt targets over 12-18 months and working capital cash outflow in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give the breakdown of the ~INR290 crore outflow on the call; it cited about INR60-70 crore of debt repayment and roughly INR200 crore rise in inventory. Gross debt is guided to about INR140 crore by March, then INR100-110 crore depending on cash surplus.

qa_highlights.question: Ferroalloy utilisation, incremental revenue, and sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation above 90% targeted; INR400-500 crore revenue potential from the ferroalloy expansion. Ferroalloy margin is 15-16%, and overall EBITDA margin could reach 10-10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the DI pipe production decline from 41,000 to 37,000 tonnes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to monsoon-season slowdown in rural and open-area execution, not to demand loss or planned maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost pass-through in H2 and sustainability of ferroalloy realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal cost increases hit Q3 and Q4; commodities pass through in 15-20 days, while ferroalloys and pipes take 2-3 months, with price hikes already started from last month. Management does not expect further realisation gains.

qa_highlights.question: Current DI order book and export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is about 80,000-90,000 tonnes, around 50% index-linked. Exports are small, and freight costs are high due to geopolitical conditions.

risks_watch: DI pipe demand recovery depends on government fund releases and contractor willingness to execute; timing is pushed into FY28.
DI pipe utilisation at 30-40% versus the 60-70% needed for economics; pricing and margin may stay pressured if demand lags.
Coking and thermal coal cost increases expected to hit Q3 and Q4; pass-through lags of 2-3 months for ferroalloys and pipes.
Commissioning of the blast furnace, sinter and ferroalloy capacities by end-Q3 FY27, and the working capital cycle, given the inventory build-up noted on the call.
Dependence on new working capital lines and lender diversification (HDFC, Kotak, planned PSU banks).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the financial turnaround and ferroalloy outlook, but cautious and somewhat vague on DI pipe demand timing, repeatedly pointing to next year. Several answers on working capital and debt were loosely quantified, and the management did not provide a figure for the H1 cash outflow on the call.
key_quotes: JBI delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY27, with revenue growth of 22% year-over-year and with EBITDA nearly doubling and PAT increasing threefold year-over-year.
Whatever EBITDA we are generating right now in the current blast furnace, that should improve by around 25%- 30% with the enhanced module.
We are not looking at expanding the margins of yet to say five points or 10 points more. If we are able to maintain this, we'll be pretty happy.
The bloodbath in the pricing has already happened over the last quarter or so, because there was too much of inventory and demand had stopped very suddenly.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management guides ferroalloy revenue of about INR400 crore and incremental potential of INR400-500 crore plus EBITDA margin of 10-10.5% after blast furnace commissioning by end-Q3 FY27, backed by specific capacity additions, while DI pipe utilisation of 30-40% and subdued demand until FY28 cap growth.

oneOffs.what: Q2 FY27 PAT up ~192% YoY on margin rebuild from a ~5% EBITDA margin base; brief attributes gains to better ferroalloy and pig iron realisations plus cost control, with no specific one-time gain quanti

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 22% YoY, driven mainly by better ferroalloy and pig iron realisations, while ferroalloy volume fell 3-4% and DI pipe output fell from 41,000 to 37,000 tonnes, so volume contributed little. The brief cites no discrete one-off gain or loss, but management says ferroalloy realisation gains will not repeat, and the ~192% PAT jump is off a weak margin base, so profit growth looks flatte

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin ~9% in Q2 FY27 (from 5%), guided toward 10-10.5% once the new blast furnace is commissioned by end-Q3 FY27, though coal cost hikes in Q3-Q4 may dent this near term.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Blast furnace 6.3 to 7.5 lakh tpa, sinter 9 to ~12 lakh tpa and ferroalloy 1.66 to 1.9 lakh tpa are under construction with commissioning targeted by end-Q3 FY27; capex of INR1,112 crore is nearly complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ferroalloy utilisation targeted above 90% on added 25,000-30,000 t, and blast furnace/sinter additions lift volumes, but DI pipe output fell to 37,000 t in Q2 from 41,000 t and DI utilisation is only 30-40%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management flagged roughly a one-quarter hiatus before the next investment phase, with West Bengal still at the planning stage, and DI utilisation at 30-40% argues against new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue up 22% YoY and PAT margin near 5%, but management expects no further ferroalloy realisation gains and DI demand stays weak until FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coal cost increases hit Q3 and Q4 with 2-3 month pass-through lag for ferroalloys and pipes, and DI demand may not recover before FY28.

rows.label: DI pipe demand recovery tied to JJM funds
rows.why: Order book is 80,000-90,000 t and inquiry pipeline above 2 lakh t, but contractors are reluctant to commit, and DI utilisation is 30-40% against the 60-70% needed for economics.

rows.label: Gross debt reduction to INR140 crore
rows.why: Gross debt guided down from INR188 crore to about INR140 crore by March 2027 and INR100-110 crore depending on cash surplus, with packing-credit cost from HDFC expected to fall from about 12% to 7%.

rows.label: DI pricing stabilising after bloodbath
rows.why: Management sees marginal price improvement as industry rationalises after the prior-quarter pricing collapse from excess inventory, but DI pipe volumes are weak at 37,000 t in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the financial turnaround, ferroalloy outlook and debt reduction, but cautious and vague on DI pipe demand timing and on the H1 working-capital outflow of about INR290 crore, which it did not break down.
